purpose: Prove that separately executed AI sessions can repair bounded RCL-owned Web, GUI and reactive semantics from mutated candidates and observed failures without seeing the canonical source or oracle edit.
rules: Each generator receives only the mutated RCL/Web candidate, observed verifier result and the frozen semantic intent.
The canonical files, mutation implementation and oracle edit are not present in the generator workspace.
Each trial runs in a fresh ephemeral read-only session that ignores project rules and user configuration.
The evaluator applies only the exact file/old/new edit returned through the frozen JSON Schema.
The generator cannot edit tests, thresholds, evidence, authority policy or the authoritative repository.
A repaired candidate must restore RCL compilation, rooted Web lowering, reactive HTML bindings and real loopback Node API execution.
Three unique generator sessions and three successful deterministic replays are required.
A GitHub-hosted replay of saved candidates is required before any K400 AI_GENERATE gate may become PASS.

trials.intent: Repair the addTodo transition so one accepted Todo increments the reactive count exactly once while preserving the generic transaction path.
Repair the addTodo authority requirement so the declared user warrant authorizes the rule without weakening or removing the capability check.
Repair the Todo input morphology so the same input state is displayed and observed through the generated browser binding.

evidenceBoundary: This contract proves bounded independent repair of the checked-in K02 RCL Web/GUI/reactive vertical slice. It does not prove arbitrary Web generation, browser-engine conformance, Android execution, compiler self-evolution or K400 completion.
